analysis: Recorded change: the proposal adds renewal_obligation, changes memory_economy and cost_escalation, redirects engine_drives_cost to a renewable-or-inherited loss, adds debt_binds_family, and changes the dread target's eliciting condition to a household discovering an unannounced renewal. Recorded change also moves earned_hope from partial remembrance to a renewal someone could refuse. Reasoned consequence: the wonder-to-dread movement is preserved but its engine becomes generational. Dread no longer arrives only as a personal erasure; it arrives as a bill the family did not know it owed, which keeps the intimacy while widening the cost beyond the surveyor. The truth-mercy dilemma becomes clearer rather than merely harsher, because a renewal can be refused: mercy is now an act with a price someone else could be asked to pay. Author decision: the review context records that the author adopted Renewal-bound debt (causal_engine, h1) from the earlier exploration. Speculative possibility: readers may experience inheritance as punishment rather than tragic obligation if the story reveals the clause too early or lets a single family absorb every consequence. That risk is not established by any recorded field and needs drafted scenes to test. The proposal does not modify the applied baseline; it remains an un-applied working revision.

recorded_observations.claim: Recorded in the proposed revision: an unrenewed memory debt passes to the family when the original contributor cannot renew.
Recorded change in the proposal: dread is elicited by a household discovering a renewal it was never told about.
Recorded change in the proposal: hope depends on someone choosing to renew a debt they could refuse, not on a clean restoration.
Recorded addition in the proposal: cost_escalation to renewal_obligation, transferring an unrenewed debt to the next generation.

hypotheses.title: Inheritance as theme
hypotheses.description: If the debt is inherited rather than only personal, the story's theme shifts from what a community owes its dead to what a household owes for a choice it did not make. That is a different thematic centre, not merely a stronger version of the old one.

uncertainties: Whether the wider cost weakens the intimate horror cannot be decided from the candidate; it needs drafted scenes.
The proposal adds an open question about who may renew on another person's behalf, and the answer would change the dilemma's fairness.
Reader experience remains an interpretation of intended effects, not an observed response.
